name: Magic Hound – APT Threat Map
description: Técnicas de Magic Hound com cobertura do catálogo (score 3=regra, 2=parcial, 1=lacuna)

techniques.comment: Magic Hound has stolen domain credentials by dumping LSASS process memory using Task Manager, comsvcs.dll, and from a Microsoft Active Directory Domain Controller using Mimikatz. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has used a web shell to exfiltrate a ZIP file containing a dump of LSASS memory on a compromised machine. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound malware gathers the victim's local IP address, MAC address, and external IP address. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has conducted a network call out to a specific website as part of their initial discovery activity. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has collected names and passwords of all Wi-Fi networks to which a device has previously connected. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has used Ping for discovery on targeted networks. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has used Remote Desktop Services to copy tools on targeted systems. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has used base64-encoded commands. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound malware has used base64-encoded files and has also encrypted embedded strings with AES. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound malware has obtained the victim username and sent it to the C2 server. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has named a malicious script CacheTask.bat to mimic a legitimate task. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has used `dllhost.exe` to mask Fast Reverse Proxy (FRP) and `MicrosoftOutLookUpdater.exe` for Plink. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has created local accounts named `help` and `DefaultAccount` on compromised machines. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has used KPortScan 3.0 to perform SMB, RDP, and LDAP scanning. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has used a tool to run `cmd /c wmic computersystem get domain` for discovery. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has used quser.exe to identify existing RDP connections. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has used scheduled tasks to establish persistence and execution. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound malware is capable of keylogging. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound malware can list running processes. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has used PowerShell for execution and privilege escalation. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has used the command-line interface for code execution. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound malware has used VBS scripts for execution. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has removed mailbox export requests from compromised Exchange servers. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has deleted and overwrote files to cover tracks. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound malware has used IRC for C2. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has used HTTP for C2. | cobertura: regra

Magic Hound enabled and used the default system managed account, DefaultAccount, via `"powershell.exe" /c net user DefaultAccount /active:yes` to connect to a targeted Exchange server over RDP. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has used domain administrator accounts after dumping LSASS process memory. | cobertura: regra

Magic Hound malware has used a PowerShell command to check the victim system architecture to determine if it is an x64 machine. Other malware has obtained the OS version, UUID, and computer/host name to send to the C2 server. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound malware can list a victim's logical drives and the type, as well the total/free space of the fixed devices. Other malware can list a directory's contents. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has used Powershell to discover email accounts. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has used Fast Reverse Proxy (FRP) for RDP traffic. | cobertura: regra

Magic Hound granted compromised email accounts read access to the email boxes of additional targeted accounts. The group then was able to authenticate to the intended victim's OWA (Outlook Web Access) portal and read hundreds of email communications for information on Middle East organizations. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has added a user named DefaultAccount to the Administrators and Remote Desktop Users groups. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound malware can use a SOAP Web service to communicate with its C2 server. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has downloaded additional code and files from servers onto victims. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has modified Registry settings for security tools. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound malware can take a screenshot and upload the file to its C2 server. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has compromised email credentials in order to steal sensitive data. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has collected .PST archives. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has exported emails from compromised Exchange servers including through use of the cmdlet `New-MailboxExportRequest.` | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has created local accounts named `help` and `DefaultAccount` on compromised machines. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has conducted watering-hole attacks through media and magazine websites. | cobertura: regra

Magic Hound has exploited the Log4j utility (CVE-2021-44228), on-premises MS Exchange servers via "ProxyShell" (CVE-2021-34473, CVE-2021-34523, CVE-2021-31207), and Fortios SSL VPNs (CVE-2018-13379). | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has attempted to lure victims into opening malicious links embedded in emails. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has attempted to lure victims into opening malicious email attachments. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has used rundll32.exe to execute MiniDump from comsvcs.dll when dumping LSASS memory. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has used a web shell to execute `nltest /trusted_domains` to identify trust relationships. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has used BitLocker and DiskCryptor to encrypt targeted workstations. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has used multiple web shells to gain execution. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound malware has used Registry Run keys to establish persistence. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has used gzip to archive dumped LSASS process memory and RAR to stage and compress local folders. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound malware has a function to determine whether the C2 server wishes to execute the newly dropped file in a hidden window. | cobertura: regra

Magic Hound has sent malicious URL links through email to victims. In some cases the URLs were shortened or linked to Word documents with malicious macros that executed PowerShells scripts to download Pupy. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound used various social media channels (such as LinkedIn) as well as messaging services (such as WhatsApp) to spearphish victims. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has used the Telegram API `sendMessage` to relay data on compromised devices. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has copied tools within a compromised network using RDP. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound malware has communicated with its C2 server over TCP ports 4443 and 10151 using HTTP. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has used Plink to tunnel RDP over SSH. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has used an encrypted http proxy in C2 communications. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has registered fraudulent domains such as "mail-newyorker.com" and "news12.com.recover-session-service.site" to target specific victims with phishing attacks. | cobertura: lacuna
Magic Hound has acquired Amazon S3 buckets to use in C2. | cobertura: lacuna
Magic Hound has used compromised domains to host links targeted to specific phishing victims. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has created fake LinkedIn and other social media accounts to contact targets and convince them--through messages and voice communications--to open malicious links. | cobertura: lacuna
Magic Hound has established email accounts using fake personas for spearphishing operations. | cobertura: lacuna
Magic Hound has compromised personal email accounts through the use of legitimate credentials and gathered additional victim information. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has obtained and used tools like Havij, sqlmap, Metasploit, Mimikatz, and Plink. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has acquired mobile phone numbers of potential targets, possibly for mobile malware or additional phishing operations. | cobertura: regra

Magic Hound gathered credentials from two victims that they then attempted to validate across 75 different websites. Magic Hound has also collected credentials from over 900 Fortinet VPN servers in the US, Europe, and Israel. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has identified high-value email accounts in academia, journalism, NGO's, foreign policy, and national security for targeting. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has captured the IP addresses of visitors to their phishing sites. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has collected location information from visitors to their phishing sites. | cobertura: lacuna
Magic Hound has captured the user-agent strings from visitors to their phishing sites. | cobertura: lacuna

Magic Hound has conducted widespread scanning to identify public-facing systems vulnerable to CVE-2021-44228 in Log4j and ProxyShell vulnerabilities; CVE-2021-26855, CVE-2021-26857, CVE-2021-26858, and CVE-2021-27065 in on-premises MS Exchange Servers; and CVE-2018-13379 in Fortinet FortiOS SSL VPNs. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has used SMS and email messages with links designed to steal credentials or track victims. | cobertura: lacuna
Magic Hound has disabled antivirus services on targeted systems in order to upload malicious payloads. | cobertura: regra
Magic Hound has executed scripts to disable the event log service. | cobertura: regra

Magic Hound has added the following rule to a victim's Windows firewall to allow RDP traffic - `"netsh" advfirewall firewall add rule name="Terminal Server" dir=in action=allow protocol=TCP localport=3389`. | cobertura: regra
